prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: insufficient (not scored)
  tan: 1.00
</profile>

TEXT_B:
Summary of Reform UK Manifesto 2024 (policy measures only)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boat crossings via detention, offshore processing, and returns; create a Department of Immigration.
- Target zero NHS waiting lists while keeping services free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; scrap energy levies and Net Zero; expand domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; ban asylum from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens; secure detention and rapid processing; immediate deportation after sentences for foreign offenders; withdraw citizenship for serious crimes.
- Restrict international students’ dependents; close abusive courses; five-year residency and employment for benefit eligibility.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise employer NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and micro-firms).
- Estimated savings £5–10bn pa; employer tax ~£4bn pa.

Government spending and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves (~£35bn pa saving).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments without cutting frontlines (~£50bn pa).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (~£6bn pa); reduce EU-derived and other regulations; improve HMRC tax collection.

Personal taxation and cost of living
- Income tax threshold to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy; scrap environmental levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above.
- Reinstate VAT-free shopping for tourists.
- Inheritance Tax: 0% under £2m; 20% above (charity option).
- Cost ~£70bn pa.

Business
- No Corporation Tax for profits under £100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% in year 3.
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; significant deregulation including employment rules; tax simplification.
- Cost ~£18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; expand UK medical training; write off fees over 10 years’ service.
- Use independent capacity domestically and abroad; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks; weekend theatres; charge for no-shows; “Pharmacy First.”
- Cost ~£17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies; remove ~£10bn pa renewable subsidies via equivalent taxation.
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas; shale test sites; SMRs and other technologies.
- Estimated savings ~£30bn pa.

Law, order, and justice
- Recruit 40,000 police over 5 years; expand stop and search; tougher sentencing for violent and drug offences; new leadership standards; phase out PCSOs; remove DEI roles.
- Justice: automatic life for violent repeat offenders; budget from £10bn to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new prison places.
- Policing cost ~£3bn pa; justice cost ~£2bn pa.

Education
- Revise curriculum; restrict gender-related interventions in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; limit undergraduate numbers; enforce entry standards.
- Strengthen free speech enforcement; expand Pupil Referral Units; offer 2-year degrees.
- Cost ~£5bn pa.

Welfare
- Tighten assessments; two-strike rule for job offers; incentives for apprenticeships and return to work. Savings ~£15bn pa.

Brexit and constitutional
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform House of Lords and Civil Service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights. Largely cost-neutral.

Defence and veterans
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay uplift; Armed Forces Justice Bill; create a Veterans Department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform; free education during/after service. Cost ~£14bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritize locals in social housing; reverse Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections. Cost-neutral.

Families and children
- Transferable marriage allowance (25%) when affordable; front-load child benefit ages 1–4; single-sex facilities; assess social media harms. Cost ~£8bn pa.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap HS2 (save ~£25bn one-off); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; no phase-out of petrol/diesel mandates; accelerate regional upgrades.
- New 50/50 public–pension fund ownership model for utilities; cap standing charges; streamline infrastructure funding. Savings ~£5bn pa (first 5 years).

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies with direct payments; reduce red tape; “Buy British” targets; CMA powers on pricing. Cost ~£2bn pa.
- Fishing: end automatic EU access; paid licences; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing; training and fleet growth. Cost ~£2bn pa.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission on social care; clamp down on offshore tax practices; pension system review; amend Mineworkers’ Pension Scheme.

Funding summary (per manifesto)
- Potential savings ~£150bn pa + £10bn pa from assumed extra growth; total ~£160bn pa.
- Total costs ~£141bn pa.

TEXT_D:
Summary of key commitments (ideological framing excluded)

- Tax, welfare and pensions:
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT.
  - Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and create an age-related personal allowance so pensioners’ tax-free threshold at least matches the State Pension.
  - Child Benefit to be based on household income: tapered between £120,000–£160,000.
  - Tackle avoidance/evasion to raise £6bn a year.
  - Welfare reforms: tighten work capability assessments, overhaul fit notes via specialist assessors, tougher sanctions at 12 months, expand UC rollout, new Fraud Bill.

- Families, childcare, education and skills:
  - 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school (by Sept 2025); nationwide wraparound care by Sept 2026; Family Hubs in every local authority.
  - Ban mobile phones during the school day; attendance measures; register for children not in school.
  - Advanced British Standard replaces A levels/T Levels; English and maths to 18; expand teacher recruitment/retention premiums.
  - 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by restricting poor‑outcome degrees; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
  - Mandatory National Service at 18: either 12‑month paid military/cyber placements (competitive) or 25 days civic service.

- Health and social care:
  - NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; +92,000 nurses and +28,000 doctors vs 2023.
  - Pharmacy First expansion; 250 new/modernised GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
  - Dental plan: 2.5m extra NHS appointments; contract reform; service requirements for newly qualified dentists; targeted “golden hellos”.
  - £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door; AI diagnostics; replace legacy IT; productivity reforms and 5,500 fewer managers.
  - Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions; implement Cass Review; single‑sex accommodation rights.

- Policing, justice and protests:
  - 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; facial recognition, knife seizure powers.
  - Harsher sentences for serious offences; four new prisons to reach 20,000 new places; expand tagging/community payback.
  - Martyn’s Law; anti-fraud measures; tighter protest controls (face coverings/pyrotechnics bans in scope).

- Immigration and borders:
  - Legal, binding annual cap on migration (work/family routes), falling each year; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks and higher IHS/insurance where needed.
  - Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights, bring Illegal Migration Act into force, process claims in 6 months, end hotel use; more returns deals; pursue treaty reforms.

- Defence and foreign:
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; at least 5% of defence budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; long‑term support to Ukraine.
  - Veterans Bill; NI waivers for dependants; improved recognition of service in benefits.

- Economy, business, infrastructure and trade:
  - Meet fiscal rules; no rise in corporation tax; maintain full expensing and consider extension to leasing; SME 10‑point plan (rates, VAT threshold review, finance access, prompt payment, regulation).
  - Digital: nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; automated vehicles law.
  - Transport: £36bn HS2 savings redeployed to regional schemes; £8.3bn potholes; Rail Reform Bill creating Great British Railways; nationwide PAYG contactless; £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.
  - Trade: complete India and GCC FTAs; implement CPTPP; maintain standards and exclude NHS from deals.

- Energy and net zero:
  - Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets; new nuclear at Wylfa; grid and connections reforms.
  - Household energy‑efficiency vouchers; maintain price cap; standing charge review; Pumpwatch; keep levies lower than 2023; no road pricing or frequent flyer levy.

- Housing and planning:
  - 1.6m homes; scrap nutrient neutrality via one‑off mitigation fee; fast‑track brownfield in 20 cities; higher London densities; development corporations; protect Green Belt.
  - Permanent FTB SDLT threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan, 5% deposit); Mortgage Guarantee continues.
  - Renters Reform (abolish s21 after court changes); leasehold reform (cap ground rents; end forfeiture; enable commonhold); 2‑year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; controls on holiday lets.

- Rural, farming, fishing, environment:
  - Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (UK‑wide, inflation‑linked); legal food security target and UK Food Security Index; fast‑track farm infrastructure; 5‑year tapered seasonal visa scheme; £20m Farming Innovation Fund.
  - Replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund; seek more inshore opportunities in 2026 talks.
  - Environment: expand Blue Belt; moratorium on deep sea mining; tougher water sector penalties/bonus bans; river recovery network; tree/peat funding; forest‑risk commodities law; new National Park; stronger waste crime penalties; limit new incinerators.

- Communities, culture and drivers:
  - £20m endowments for 105 towns (plus more); extend Community Ownership Fund and UKSPF; more Freeports/Investment Zones.
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local votes on LTNs/20mph.
  - Maintain grassroots sport investment; Independent Football Regulator; creative tax incentives; BBC funding review and new complaints process.

- Sex and gender law:
  - Clarify Equality Act: “sex” means biological; one legal sex in UK law; statutory school guidance on gender‑questioning pupils with parental involvement.

- Union and devolution:
  - Protect internal market; extend UKSPF/towns/community funds to devolved nations; targeted transport/energy projects in Scotland, Wales, NI; implement Windsor Framework and legacy arrangements in NI.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile.
